[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Shared VPC service-project association may be created before this project's Compute API is enabled. It has no dependency on the API-enablement resources, while `google_project_service.project_services` is the resource that activates configured services; make the association wait for it.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Shared VPC service-project association requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled for the service project first. Unlike the host-project association, this resource has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`; add an explicit dependency so the association is not attempted before API activation completes.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Shared VPC service-project association should wait for the project's APIs to be enabled. Unlike the host-project resource and the other API-dependent setup resources, this resource has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`; attempting to associate the service project before Compute API enablement can fail.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches the project as a Shared VPC service project to the host project, which is done through the Compute Engine API on the service project. It has no dependency on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`, so the Compute API may not be enabled yet when the attachment is attempted (its sibling `google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host` correctly depends on the service enablement). Because `service_project` comes from a local string there is no clean data-reference fix; add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches this project to a Shared VPC host as a service project, which requires the Compute Engine API (compute.googleapis.com) to be enabled on the service project first. Unlike its sibling `google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host` (which has `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`), this resource has no `depends_on` and references only the project id via `local.project.project_id`, never `google_project_service.project_services`. It can therefore run before the API is enabled and fail. Add an explicit `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the service project first. Unlike the host-side resources (shared_vpc_host -> service_projects) which chain to google_project_service.project_services, shared_vpc_service has no attribute reference or depends_on to project_services, so nothing guarantees the Compute Engine API is enabled before the attachment. Add depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services].

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project to an external host, but has no dependency on the project's API enablement. Google requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the service project before it can be attached to a Shared VPC host. When compute.googleapis.com is in var.services, both resources are created in parallel with no ordering edge (the only dependency via local.project covers the project's existence, not its enabled services), so the attachment can run before (or without) the API being enabled and fail intermittently. An explicit depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services] on the shared_vpc_service resource is needed; no clean data-reference alternative exists since service_project is already fully determined by local.project.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the service project. API enablement (google_project_service.project_services) is asynchronous, but this resource has no dependency on it — unlike the host-side counterpart google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host, which does declare depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]. Without the dependency the attachment can race ahead of API enablement and fail intermittently.
